clue.text: Panic to make homes secure

parts.note: flats are homes, apartments in a block
to pin something is to fasten or secure it

explanation.surface: A frightened householder rushes to lock up the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat spin is an aircraft's uncontrolled horizontal rotation, used figuratively for a state of agitated confusion.

clue.text: Imperfect system of rules introduced by US bank

indicators.note: the system of rules is brought into the bank's name, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: the Fed is the US Federal Reserve, America's central bank
law is a system of rules

explanation.surface: A complaint that the regulations brought in by an American bank are flawed.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawed is a near synonym of imperfect: having a defect or fault.

clue.text: A work of art, when mounted, creates disturbance

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting something makes it go upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a mural is a work of art painted on a wall

explanation.surface: A painting causes a stir once it is hung on the gallery wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when mounted' turns MURAL upwards to LARUM, which follows A; 'creates' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarum is an old word for an alarm or call to arms, hence a commotion.

clue.text: European translation of antinovel's timeless

indicators.note: translating a text renders it into new form, so these letters are rearranged
being without time means the abbreviation T for time is dropped from the letters

parts.note: the word with its S, read as antinovel is

explanation.surface: A remark about a foreign version of an experimental novel lacking any sense of period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' takes T out of ANTINOVELS, leaving ANINOVELS, and 'translation of' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slovenian is a person from Slovenia, a country of central Europe, so a European.

clue.text: Lack of concern shown during dispute

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
a difference is a disagreement or dispute, as in 'settle their differences'

explanation.surface: Someone shrugged their shoulders while an argument was going on.
explanation.definitionFit: Indifference is apathy, not caring one way or the other.

clue.text: Priests holding mass for harvest celebration of yore

indicators.note: the priests' word holds the letter for mass inside it

parts.note: lamas are Buddhist priests or monks of Tibet
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Clergy celebrate a service to give thanks for the crops in olden days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Priests holding mass' looks like a Christian service, but the priests are Tibetan lamas and mass is just the letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: Lammas, 1 August, was the old English feast of the first wheat harvest, when loaves were blessed.

clue.text: A teacher can be wrong

parts.note: Miss is how schoolchildren address a female teacher

explanation.surface: A suggestion that teachers are fallible too.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means faulty or out of order, as in 'something is amiss'.

clue.text: Film star briefly seen travelling through African city

indicators.note: said briefly, the name is cut short by losing its final letter

parts.note: Marilyn Monroe was a Hollywood film star
via means by way of, travelling through a place

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star is glimpsed passing through an African capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Monrovia is the capital city of Liberia in West Africa.

clue.text: Supporter of Queen Elizabeth II

parts.note: the Roman numeral two, in a regnal name, is read as second
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A royalist declares their loyalty to the late monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the order 'Elizabeth II' reverses: SECOND for II, then ER for the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A seconder backs a motion proposed at a meeting, giving it formal support.

clue.text: According to report, girl outwitted a killer

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: the girl's name Anna, conned for outwitted, then a, spoken together

explanation.surface: News that a young woman got the better of a murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a huge South American constricting snake that crushes its prey to death.

clue.text: During discussion, choose to take food outside

indicators.note: in discussion words are spoken, so the clue relies on their sound

parts.note: pick means choose and nick means take or steal; said together

explanation.surface: While chatting, someone opts to eat out in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnic is a meal eaten outdoors, often on a rug in a park.

clue.text: Breed of dog, barker biting train er nastily

indicators.note: the barker's word bites into, or holds in its jaws, the other letters

parts.note: a crier is someone who calls out loudly, like a fairground barker

indicators.note: doing something nastily twists it about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog breed snapping at a trainer who is cruel to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nastily' rearranges TRAINER to AIRNTER, which 'biting' places inside CRIER after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: The cairn terrier is a small shaggy Scottish terrier, bred to hunt among rock piles.

clue.text: English duet rewritten as short musical piece

indicators.note: something rewritten is put into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An English piece for two players is rearranged as a brief composition.
explanation.definitionFit: An etude is a short instrumental study composed to practise a technique.

clue.text: Tries to stop standards getting lower

parts.note: a standard is a flag or banner
down means lower, in a lower position

explanation.surface: Someone resists the decline in standards.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag down a car or taxi is to wave at it to try to make it halt.

clue.text: Safety procedure carried out in rifle range?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a rifle range is where the safety drill takes place.
explanation.walkthrough: Fire here is first the blaze an evacuation drill prepares for, then the shooting practised at a range.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal of building evacuation is held for emergencies; firing at targets is the shooting practice done at a rifle range.

clue.text: Ill-tempered note put end to harmony

parts.note: a crotchet is a musical note, a quarter note

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, taken here from the word harmony

explanation.surface: A grumpy musician hits a note that ruins the harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: Crotchety means irritable and grumpy, especially of an old person.

clue.text: Lifted lid on heroine's predicaments

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it
in a down clue lifting raises the word so it reads upwards

parts.note: Emma is the heroine of Jane Austen's novel of that name; with the S as written

explanation.surface: A secret uncovered about a heroine's troubles, as if raising a lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted' turns LID upwards to DIL, which sits 'on' EMMAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is an awkward situation offering a choice between equally unwelcome options.

clue.text: Sent to bed, hurried along

explanation.definitionFit: To scuttle a ship is to sink it deliberately to the seabed; to scuttle is also to scurry along with short quick steps.

clue.text: Plan to adopt party member having a chance of success

indicators.note: adopting something takes it in, so the plan word takes the member inside

parts.note: an intention is a plan or aim
Con is short for a Conservative, a member of that British political party

explanation.surface: A plan to take on a political figure who might win.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in contention means being among those who could still win a contest.

clue.text: Find water wonderful

explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to dowse, seeking underground water with a rod; divine is also an informal word for delightful or heavenly.

clue.text: Artist's bunker, might one say?

definitions.note: read as artist is, the 's standing for is

indicators.note: asking what one might say points to how the words sound when spoken

parts.note: a war hole, a hole dug for shelter in war, describes a bunker

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a painter's studio is really a fortified shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy Warhol was the American pop painter of soup cans and Marilyn prints.

clue.text: Motor race rerouted, bypassing country

indicators.note: going round something, so one word goes round the other
a rerouted course is sent another way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: A motor race diverted to avoid crossing a nation's border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rerouted' turns RACE into ECAR, and 'bypassing' sends it round STATE: E-STATE-CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor is British for a car, and an estate car is the British name for a station wagon.

clue.text: Discuss much-reduced theatre attendance

indicators.note: cutting the two words down a great deal leaves only a short run of letters from their middle

explanation.surface: Talk about falling audiences at the playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat a subject is to deal with or write about it.

clue.text: Half portion of toast served by a friend

indicators.note: the first piece is followed or attended by the next one
half of the word's letters, the front portion of it, is taken

parts.note: chin-chin is an old-fashioned drinking toast

explanation.surface: A chum brings out half a slice of toast.
explanation.walkthrough: CHINA is a friend in Cockney rhyming slang: china plate, mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with mate, a pal.

clue.text: Starfish in Barnet?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a starfish has got tangled in someone's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNET is Cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair), so 'in Barnet?' points to a hairstyle; in heraldry a star is called a mullet.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a five-pointed star charge; also an edible sea fish; and a haircut short at front, long at the back.

clue.text: See one die like a snake

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see, as used in references
I is the Roman numeral for one
to perish is to die

explanation.surface: Watching someone expire like a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Viperish means spiteful and venomous, behaving in the manner of a viper.

clue.text: Drug — speed —- regularly consumed

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter of the word speed

parts.note: ate means consumed, eaten

explanation.surface: A warning about the amphetamine called speed being taken habitually.
explanation.definitionFit: To sedate someone is to calm them with a drug, giving a sedative.

clue.text: Sea creature, unusually large? Yes

indicators.note: done unusually means in an odd way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether a sea animal is unusually big, and answering yes.
explanation.definitionFit: The grey seal is a large seal of North Atlantic coasts, common around Britain.
